assumptions: Onset was placed at 22:39 from the first ZeroDivisionError log line and the first minute showing mixed flag evaluations; the flag provider's own change timestamp was not read back, so the exact toggle time is inferred.

Causation between the flag toggle and the failures is inferred from correlation (error type changed at the same minute the flag flipped, and recovered within a minute of the revert). It was not proven by reproducing the defect.

The conclusion that no code change was involved rests on the change-event query returning zero deploys/releases for io-shop in the prior 24 hours. A change made outside that window, on a dependency, or through a channel not covered by that query would not have appeared.

The low-level UpstreamTimeout errors present throughout the hour before onset are assumed to be pre-existing background noise, unrelated to this incident, and are assumed to still be present after mitigation.
Who toggled the flag, and whether the toggle was intentional or part of a planned rollout, was not established. No guard was identified that would prevent the same toggle from being made again.

The second candidate cause (a latent defect in the primary path) was never tested. It is not mutually exclusive with the confirmed cause and is treated here as the standing risk: the mitigation restored the fallback path but left the defective primary path in place.
The proposed fix is an unreviewed draft pull request; it is assumed to address the defect but has not been verified or merged.

Impact was assessed only through the service's own error-rate logs and the alert. No customer-facing or downstream impact assessment was performed, and the account page is assumed to be the only affected surface.
input.executive_summary: On the evening of 15 September 2026, a configuration switch controlling which checkout code the online shop uses was turned off. From that moment, a share of customers loading their account page received an error instead of the page; the rest of the site's traffic was unaffected. The failures began at 22:39 UTC, automated monitoring raised an alert at 22:44, and the on-call automation restored the previous setting at 22:45. The site was confirmed back to its normal behaviour at 22:46, about seven minutes after customers first saw errors and roughly one minute after the alert was picked up. No data was lost; affected customers would have seen a failed page load and could retry successfully after the fix. The underlying software defect that the switch exposed has not been fixed — a draft code change has been proposed for review, and until it is merged the older code path is the only safe configuration.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` was turned off at 22:39, which routed account page requests onto the primary (new checkout) code path, where a latent division-by-zero defect raised ZeroDivisionError on every affected request. No deploy or release was recorded on io-shop in the 24 hours before onset, so the defect was exposed by the flag change rather than introduced by a code change; the bug still exists in the primary path and would recur the next time the flag is turned off.
